newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SKODA SAYS JAN-OCT TOTAL SALES UP.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SKODA SAYS JAN-OCT TOTAL SALES UP.

text.p: Czech Skoda Auto a.s., a unit of Germany's Volkswagen AG, on Thursday said its total sales for January-October were up 25 percent, year-on-year, to 214,000 automobiles.
A Skoda statement said that sales in October alone were some 36 percent higher than the previous year at 24,496 cars.
It added that sales for the Czech Republic alone for the first 10 months were also up about 25 percent, year-on-year, to 71,378 cars.

Germany was the largest importer of Skoda's during the period at 17,879 autos, followed by Slovakia (17,793), Poland (12,462), Great Britain (11,963), Austria (8,179), France (7,933) and Italy (7,494).
The statement said that sales to Italy in October soared to 1,017 cars from 163 in October 1995, "thanks mainly to our assembly plant in Poland".
In 1994 it opened an assembly plant in Poznan, Poland which produced 7,857 vehicles last year. Skoda said it would like to raise this number to at least 14,000 vehicles.
Skoda has said it expects to break even or post a small profit this year, improving from a 1.6 billion crown loss in 1995.

Volkswagen, according to a privatisation agreement with the Czech goverment, originally took a stake in Skoda in 1992, and increasing its holdings in Skoda to 70 percent last year from 60.3 percent under the deal.
